hook: My landlord says a **verbal deal** is enough. Is it?
hook_q: Do I need a written rent agreement?

slides.title: Over **one year?** Register it.
slides.body: A lease from year to year, for any term over one year, or reserving a yearly rent can be made only by a registered instrument.
slides.ref: Transfer of Property Act 1882 · Sec 107; Registration Act 1908 · Sec 17(1)(d)

slides.title: Shorter leases: **oral can work.**
slides.body: All other leases may be made either by a registered instrument or by an oral agreement accompanied by delivery of possession.
slides.note: State rent laws may add rules

slides.title: Registered deed? **Both** sign.
slides.body: Where a lease is made by a registered instrument, it must be executed by both the lessor (landlord) and the lessee (tenant).

slides.title: Not registered? It **may not count.**
slides.body: A lease that had to be registered but wasn't does not affect the property and can't be used as evidence of the deal. It may still prove a collateral transaction.

slides.title: Stamp duty and rent laws: **your State.**
list: States set stamp duty rates on leases
Landlord and tenant relations are on the State List
So check your State's stamp and rent laws
slides.ref: Constitution · Seventh Schedule, List II Entries 18, 63; List I Entry 91

slides.title: Model Tenancy Act? **Only a model.**
slides.body: In 2021 the Centre circulated a Model Tenancy Act to States and UTs, to adopt by enacting fresh laws or amending their rental laws. Check what your State has done.

sources: Constitution of India – Seventh Schedule, List I Entry 91, List II Entries 18, 63
Press Information Bureau (pib.gov.in) – Model Tenancy Act, 2 June 2021 and 25 July 2022
caption:
Renting a home on a handshake? Here's when the law needs it in writing. 👇

1️⃣ A lease for more than one year, year to year, or with a yearly rent can be made only by a registered instrument
2️⃣ Other leases can be oral, if possession is handed over, or by a registered instrument (your State's rent or registration law may add rules)
3️⃣ A registered lease must be signed by both landlord and tenant
4️⃣ A lease that had to be registered but wasn't can't affect the property or be used as evidence of the deal
5️⃣ Stamp duty and rent-control rules depend on your State
6️⃣ The Model Tenancy Act, 2021 is a model for States, not a law everywhere

Source: Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Sec 105, 107); Registration Act, 1908 (Sec 17, 49); Constitution, Seventh Schedule; PIB
